messages:
alex: Heads-up — saw a spike in preempt evictions in us-west-2 this morning. A few streaming responses got cut mid-token. Need quick sync on runtime handling so clients don't have to re-gen full responses.
priya: Logs? any pattern (model, seq len, instance type)?
jia: Most hits were on longer streaming chats (16k window) on preemptible g5s. eviction events cluster around capacity reclaim windows.
alex: infra-bot attached the event bundle. Node term, then clients hit truncated stream frames.
infra-bot: eviction: node-ps-233 terminated (preempt). reason: capacity_reclaim. affected: 18 requests streaming. ts=2026-03-18T08:14:22Z
sam: We should avoid forcing clients to re-request whole output. Options I see: 1) server-side resume token + requeue, 2) streaming proxy that can replay cached tokens, 3) dual-write tokens to a cheap store while streaming so fallback resumes mid-stream.
jia: Dual-write per-token is expensive (RT writes). Maybe we checkpoint every N tokens (2s / 32 tokens) and on eviction requeue with prefix cached.
priya: Idea: handshake-driven cutover. On eviction signal runtime switches stream -> HANDOFF, flushes current KV cache to shared store, emits a final frame with a resume_id, then detaches. Fallback worker takes resume_id, preloads prefix cache and continues. Client lib will reopen connection with resume_id header.
alex: Implementation sketch: graceful_drain_window = 6s; checkpoint_interval = 2s or 32 tokens; resume_ttl = 60s in redis; resume header = 'X-Resume-Id'. Fallback lookup by resume-id. Fall back to full regen if not found.
sam: Pseudocode snippet:
```
// eviction handler (pseudocode)
on_eviction() {
  set_stream_mode('HANDOFF')
  flush_kv(prefix_cache)
  resume_id = store_resume(prefix_cache)
  emit_frame({resume_id, partial_done:true})
  sleep(2000) // allow client ack
  drain_connections()
  exit(0)
}
```
jia: Edgecases: client ack might not arrive before process is reaped. Also tool-calls / external side-effects in-progress — we need idempotency.
priya: Mitigations: client library should attempt reconnect + check resume store by request_id if no resume_id frame received. Also we can include a short-lived control-plane webhook for resume-ack but that's heavier.
alex: Metrics to add: resume_attempts, resume_success_rate, resume_latency, tokens_recovered, fallback_cost. SLO suggestion: >= 99.5% of interrupted streams resume without full re-gen.
sam: Cost tradeoff: fallback to Dedicated/on-demand for in-flight resumption will cost more but saves latency and customer UX. Mixed-pool buffer: infra could keep 8–10% on-demand headroom for long streams.
infra-bot: capacity tip: bump mixed-pool on-demand buffer to 10% during peak windows to reduce evictions for long-running streams.
priya: Owner: sam (eng-runtime). Reviewers: jia, alex (infra). Timeline: PoC 2w -> canary 1w -> rollout gated on resume_success >= 99% on canary.
alex: Next step: sam to open RFC + PoC branch. Include: redis schema, resume-id format, client handshake, metrics to emit, and canary playbook. Tag @oncall when canary scheduled.
oncall-bot: Reminder: schedule canary outside high-traffic window (avoid 09:00–11:00 PST). create ephemeral alert: resume_fail_rate > 0.5% for 30m.
sam: Will do. I'll start RFC and mock client changes. Thanks all :thumbsup:
